title: Distributed multi-GPU throughput harness for tensor+pipeline parallel stacks
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: build a reproducible, CI-driven harness to measure end-to-end inference throughput (tokens/sec) and tail latency (p95, p99) for multi-GPU setups that use tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and hybrid topologies. The harness should detect regressions against baseline metrics, surface model-config-level trade-offs (batch size, micro-batch, KV cache behavior), and produce artifactable reports for perf-owners and SREs. Scope covers 8->128 GPU clusters across supported instance types and both NCCL and RPC-based interconnects. This ticket covers design, reference implementation, CI integration, and a first pass of regression rules/alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible script to run end-to-end throughput tests for at least three model configs: 7B (sharded), 70B (tensor+pipeline), and a 100B pipeline-only reference.
Automated calculation of tokens/sec, p95 and p99 latency per stage, and aggregated end-to-end p95 across requests.
Baseline store and comparator that can detect >5% regression in tokens/sec or >10% increase in p95 and emit a structured failure in CI.
Artifacts: per-run CSV, flamegraph/trace link, and a compact summary JSON plus markdown report uploaded to Confluence/drive link.
Runbook entry for how to interpret failures and recommended remediation steps (e.g., kernel rollout, NCCL tuning, micro-batch changes).
design_notes: Use a controller-worker pattern: controller schedules synthetic and replay workloads to a test cluster, collects KV cache hit stats and per-GPU throughput counters.
Prefer real prompt traces for tail-latency measurement and synthetic dense-token streams for saturated throughput numbers.
Measure both steady-state (sustained streaming) and spike (burst fan-out) workloads; capture warmup windows for KV cache population.
Expose knobs: tensor-parallel degree, pipeline stages, micro-batch size, sequence length distribution, quantization profile.
Keep kernel-selection deterministic for baseline runs; record kernel/version metadata to make regressions attributable to runtime or model changes.
test_plan: Testbed: dedicate 8xA100-80GB, 32xA100 (multi-node), and a 64xH100 cluster for high-end runs. Record NCCL versions, driver, and OS kernel.

Workloads: (1) Synthetic uniform 1k token streams at batch sizes [1,4,8,16], (2) Replay of production prompt corpus sampled from anonymized telemetry, (3) KV-heavy long-context test to exercise cache coherence.
Metrics collection: per-GPU throughput counters, inter-GPU PCIe/NIC utilization, NCCL op durations, KV cache hit/miss ratios, and trace spans for pipeline stages.
Regression detection: compare new-run summary to baseline via percent-diff and statistical test; flag persistent regressions across 3 consecutive CI runs before auto-filing an incident ticket.
infra_required: dedicated test clusters (list in Confluence), provisioning automation via infra-playbooks
access to perf NVMe scratch for traces
CI runner with multi-node networking and GPU passthrough
storage bucket for artifacts with lifecycle policy
